question: Can a frozen learned decoder compose received answers to cover an unseen nonlinear relation and recognize when a one-source change makes a fourth bit necessary?
inputs: Four anonymous signed-clause questions on nine source bits. The sender sees the raw values; both endpoints know the public incidence and the earlier frozen question parser.
forbidden_inputs: Held examples, target query names, teacher circuits, omitted port, family identifiers, raw values at the receiver, grader or transmission metadata at deployment. No fitting after checkpoint freeze.
outputs: A fixed-width three- or four-bit packet sent before the requested port is known. An omitted answer is reconstructed by a NAND circuit on the packet.
mapping: Fit a library of binary NAND programs and a public probe budget on other relations. Plan by composing the frozen programs on packet slots. Report both unchecked proposals and independently certified returns.
primary_observable: All four delayed queries exact on all 512 inputs, with three bits on the closed nonlinear wiring and four on the open wiring, against an exact cached functional-dependency compiler.
comparators_or_controls: Parity-only shortcut, no composition, exact public lookup compiler and four-answer transmission, training relation symmetry check, event-level independent audit. Separate actual empirical savings from supplied search and checking.
resource_budget: One finite program fit on even-parity input examples. All test layouts run on all 512 states. Compare verified setup and ordinary traffic at 1, 16, 256, 4096 and 65536 uses per wiring.
first_executable_signal: A nonlinear held answer is computed correctly from three transmitted answers without seeing the raw input at the decoder.
stop_rule: Score the frozen primary policies and controls on every predeclared menu. Keep a failed raw proposal even when the certificate recovers an exact result.
nonclaims: Finite delayed-query protocol. Timing is specific to the stated implementation and host. No general program-learning, complexity or recursive improvement claim.
